q: how do I know if my child is getting dehydrated from vomiting
text:
The main risk from vomiting is dehydration, according to the SEUP [1]. Signs that your child is getting worse and needs to be seen again include vomiting a lot, not keeping down solids or liquids, or vomiting even when they take nothing [5]. Vomiting that is green, contains blood, or looks like brown coffee grounds also needs medical attention [5].

To prevent dehydration, offer oral rehydration solution: wait 20 minutes after a vomit, then give 2–5 ml every 5 minutes for an hour, and increase gradually if it is well tolerated [4]. Do not use homemade solutions or commercial soft drinks [4]. If your child is listless, vomits many times, or will not take liquids, see your doctor [1].

q: my 5 year old has been coughing all night, what can I do
text:
A cough that lasts more than a week is common with a cold, and the cough can outlast the other symptoms, according to the SEUP [4]. Keep giving plenty of fluids, and for a young child you can do nasal washes with saline before feeds and before bed, never with tap water [4]. Keep your child away from smoke and from places where people are smoking [4]. Do not use cough syrups or other cold medicines, especially in children under 6 years old [4].

See a doctor if your child is breathing faster, the ribs or chest are pulling in, or they are struggling to swallow or drooling a lot [1].

q: my son has been coughing for a week after a cold
text:
A cough that lingers after a cold is common, and cold symptoms can last 10 to 14 days, according to MedlinePlus [6]. If the cough comes in bouts that are worse at night, or your son makes a "whoop" sound gasping between coughs, it may be whooping cough — its first signs are like a cold, and the cough can then last several weeks or months [4]. In whooping cough the cough usually becomes more severe after about a week, with coughing fits that can make it hard to breathe or cause vomiting [1].

See a doctor if he is getting worse, struggling to breathe, or not getting better.

q: he has a cough but no fever and is eating normally
text:
A cough without a fever, with normal eating, is usually not a sign of anything serious in a child who is otherwise well. A high temperature is the body's natural response to fighting infections like coughs and colds, according to the NHS [1]. Most fevers are benign and self-limiting, and fever alone rarely causes complications, according to the AEPap [5]. Keep offering fluids and let them rest.

See a doctor if your child stops eating, is not their usual self, seems dehydrated, or has a fever lasting 5 days or more [1].

q: my daughter has red spots all over her stomach and they appeared today
text:
Red spots that appear suddenly can have several causes, and most are not serious. A common one in children is a viral infection, which spreads easily, so handwashing with soap before meals and after using the toilet helps prevent it, according to the SEUP [3]. Keep an eye on how she seems in herself, and let her keep to her normal activity if she is comfortable [4].

See a doctor if she is generally unwell, limp, pale, or refusing food and drink [6].

q: my 2 year old has little red bumps on his legs and keeps scratching them
text:
Itchy red bumps on the legs can have several common causes, and the pattern matters more than the bumps alone. In scabies, itching is intense and often worse at night, with bumps and lines on the fingers, wrists, arms, legs and around the waist, according to the WHO [1]. Eczema causes dry, itchy skin with a rash, and scratching can make it redder and itchier; it is not contagious [2]. Hives are raised, itchy patches or bumps that vary in size and can appear on the legs [3].

See your doctor if the itching is severe, the skin looks infected, or your child seems unwell.

q: these spots dont seem to bother her but there are more every morning
text:
Spots that don't bother her and keep appearing each morning are common with nappy rash, which can usually be treated at home, according to the NHS [2]. It can look like red or raw patches on the bottom or the whole nappy area, or spots, pimples or blisters that may be red or brown and are harder to see on brown and black skin [2]. Some babies are uncomfortable or distressed with it, but not all are [2].

See your doctor if the rash spreads, blisters, or does not improve with simple home care [2].

q: my 6 year old fell from the bed and hit the back of his head
text:
Most head injuries in children are not serious, according to the NHS [2]. After a blow to the head, the usual symptoms are headache, confusion, brief memory loss, dizziness, nausea, vomiting and drowsiness, according to the SEUP [1].

Watch him over the next 24 hours for warning signs [3]. Get urgent medical help if he has been knocked out, cannot stay awake, has a seizure, is vomiting repeatedly, is confused or hard to wake, has clear fluid or blood from the nose or ears, has trouble walking or speaking, or if his behaviour changes [2][4]. Because he fell from a bed, which is less than a metre, that alone does not require emergency care [5].

Let him rest from physical and mental activity for 24 to 48 hours, then return gradually to normal activities [4]. He can eat normally and can sleep, though after a more significant knock it is worth waking him every 4 hours [6]. If he has a headache, acetaminophen or ibuprofen can be given in the dose your doctor indicates [6].

q: what foods should I start with for a baby who just turned 6 months
text: Around 6 months, milk alone no longer meets a baby's energy and nutrient needs, so solid foods should start now, according to the WHO [1]. Begin with small amounts and increase them gradually as your baby grows, and build up the variety and texture of foods over time [1]. Offer 2 to 3 meals a day at this age, alongside frequent breastfeeding or formula [1]. Give one new food at a time so you can spot any allergic reaction, such as a rash, diarrhoea or vomiting, according to MedlinePlus [5]. Do not give honey before the first birthday, and avoid cow's milk and unpasteurised foods before then [5]. Ask your pediatrician if you have questions about starting solids [5].

q: my baby refuses vegetables but eats fruit all day
text: Fruit is fine, but it should not replace vegetables: the AEP advises introducing the whole variety of fruits and vegetables progressively, at any daily meal, and varying how they are offered — puréed, mashed or in small pieces [3]. Taste for different flavours, including bitter ones like some vegetables, is built from an early age, and early exposure to different flavours may reduce the risk of refusing new foods [3]. Fruit juices offer no nutritional benefit over whole fruit and can displace other foods, so whole fruit is recommended [3]. Keep offering vegetables without forcing, alongside what your baby already likes.

q: my daughter is 13 months and still mostly drinks formula
text: At 13 months, formula alone no longer covers what she needs: around 6 months, energy and nutrient needs start to exceed what milk provides, so complementary foods are needed [2]. The WHO recommends continuing breastfeeding up to 2 years or beyond while introducing nutritionally adequate and safe solid foods from 6 months [3]. Complementary feeding means giving solid or liquid foods alongside milk — not instead of it [6]. From 9 to 23 months, offer 3–4 meals a day, plus 1–2 snacks if needed [2]. If you are worried about how much she is eating, talk to your doctor.

q: how often should a newborn poop
text: It is normal for a newborn's pooping to vary a lot from baby to baby: the rhythm and consistency of stools differ from one person to another, and a child does not have to poop every day, according to the SEUP [3]. What matters more than the number is the consistency — constipation is when stools become too hard, with discomfort or incomplete pooping, and it can come with fewer stools than usual [6]. In a baby under 6 months, keep feeding as usual with breast milk or formula [3]. See your doctor if there is blood in the stool, a lot of tummy pain, or repeated vomiting with poor feeding [3].

q: my 9 month old suddenly wakes up every two hours at night
text: Waking at night is normal at this age: night wakings are physiological, and around 30% of children still wake at night by their first birthday, according to the PUC Chile manual [1]. Each sleep cycle lasts about 90 minutes, so brief wakings between cycles are expected [1]. If your baby always falls asleep in your arms, they may need the same conditions to fall back asleep on their own [1]. Most infant insomnia is due to habits rather than illness, and it does not affect growth [4]. If your baby seems unwell, snores heavily, or the wakings come with fever or poor feeding, see your doctor.

q: my 4 year old wakes up coughing only when he lies down
text:
A cough that comes mainly at night is one of the symptoms of asthma in children, according to MedlinePlus [5]. Other signs can include chest tightness, wheezing when breathing out, shortness of breath, feeling tired or irritable, and trouble eating [5]. In preschool children, viral respiratory infections are the main cause of wheezing, and asthma can be hard to diagnose at this age because it looks like other childhood conditions [1][6].

See a doctor if your child has severe coughing, serious breathing problems, or turns pale or blue in the face, lips or nails [5].

q: my son has asthma and is using albuterol more than usual
text: Using a reliever inhaler more often than usual is a sign the asthma is not well controlled, and the treatment plan may need reviewing. According to the WHO, treatment depends on how frequent the symptoms are, and many people with asthma need to use an inhaler every day [2]. A spacer makes the medicine reach the lungs better, especially for children [2]. Most asthma flare-ups are mild and can be managed at home with bronchodilators, though symptoms can last up to a week, according to the SEUP [3]. See your doctor if he is needing his inhaler more than usual, so his plan can be checked.

q: she is making a strange noise when she breathes but is still smiling
text:
A strange noise when breathing can be a sign of croup, which is an inflammation of the vocal cords and windpipe that causes noisy, high-pitched breathing and a barking cough, according to MedlinePlus [3]. It often starts like a cold and the symptoms usually get worse at night, lasting three to five days [3]. Most viral cases are mild and can be treated at home, but if you are worried about your child's breathing, call your doctor right away [3].

Watch for difficulty breathing — ribs pulling in, the chest sinking, fast breathing, or tiredness — and see a doctor if that appears [1][4].

q: my 4 year old had a seizure when he was a baby, does that change anything now
text:
A febrile seizure is not usually serious and is unlikely to have harmed your child or caused long-term effects, according to the NHS [2]. They usually affect children between 6 months and 6 years old, and most last 2 to 3 minutes [5]. Having had one does not mean your child has epilepsy, though children who have had a febrile seizure have a slightly increased chance of epilepsy later in life, which is rare [3]. You cannot prevent febrile seizures [3].

If your child has another seizure, keep them safe while you wait for medical help: check the time it starts and ends, protect their head with your hands or something soft, and move dangerous objects away [4]. After it ends, put them in the recovery position and make sure nothing is in their mouth or throat [4]. Do not hold them in place or put anything in their mouth [1].

Get medical help if a seizure lasts more than 5 minutes, they have trouble breathing, the stiffness and twitching is on only one side, they are more sleepy than usual for over an hour afterwards, or they have more than one seizure within 24 hours [5].

A 4-month-old should be wetting diapers frequently, with clear, odourless urine — especially if they are breastfed only, according to MedlinePlus [4]. The number of wet diapers a day varies a lot from baby to baby, so what matters is the pattern, not an exact count [4].

q: can babies get dehydrated from breastfeeding
banner: 🚨 With these symptoms your child should be seen in the emergency department today, without waiting. | Reason: Signs of dehydration: sunken eyes, little urine, dry mouth, persistent vomiting or heavy diarrhoea >24 h
text: Yes, a baby who is breastfeeding can become dehydrated, because dehydration happens when more fluid is lost than taken in [2]. In babies, the common causes are diarrhoea, vomiting and fever [2]. Breastfeeding is protective and should continue: keep breastfeeding normally, and even more often if the baby wants it [1]. Exclusive breastfeeding for the first six months also helps prevent diarrhoeal illness [4]. If your baby has diarrhoea or vomiting, oral rehydration solution is what replaces the water and salts lost [4][5], and it should be given in small amounts often [5]. Signs of dehydration need medical care, and your baby should be seen today.

text:
No, DTaP is not the vaccine for an 11-year-old: it is only for children younger than 7 years old, and different vaccines against tetanus, diphtheria and pertussis (Tdap and Td) are used for older children, adolescents and adults, according to MedlinePlus [1].

q: my toddler has a swollen eyelid after waking up
text:
A swollen eyelid on waking can be one of the early signs of roseola, a very common infection in babies and toddlers, according to the NHS [3]. In roseola it appears together with a sudden high temperature, cold-like symptoms such as a sore throat, runny nose and cough, and swollen glands in the neck, and these last 3 to 5 days before a rash comes out [3]. The rash is made of pinkish-red spots or bumps, starts on the chest, tummy and back and then spreads to the face, neck and arms, and usually fades within 2 days [3]. You can normally look after your child at home and they should recover within a week [3].

See a doctor if your child has trouble breathing or makes a noise when breathing, drools, has blue lips, looks pale, or loses consciousness [5].

q: my 2 year old weighs 40 pounds, should I be worried
text:
40 lb = 18.1 kg.

Whether a 2-year-old's weight is a concern depends on their height, not on weight alone. For children under 5, the WHO defines overweight as a weight-for-height more than two standard deviations above the median, and obesity as more than three [4]. So the same weight can be normal in a tall child and a concern in a shorter one. The WHO also advises against putting young children on restrictive diets while they are still growing [1]. Ask your doctor to plot your child's weight and height on the growth chart and tell you how they are tracking.

Note: 18.1 kg is very high for a child of 2 years on the WHO growth charts. If it was a typo, correct it, because doses go by weight; if it is right, mention it to your doctor.

The SEUP says most cases are mild and get better within a few days, sometimes up to a week [4].

Keep an eye on your child's breathing and their colour and general condition, as the SEUP advises [4]. If you are worried about your child's breathing, contact your doctor right away [1].

q: my son has a rash after swimming in a lake
text:
An itchy rash of raised bumps or patches that can appear anywhere on the body and look pink or red is typical of hives, according to the NHS [2]. In childhood, most hives are caused by an infection, and an allergic cause is less common, according to the SEUP [1]. The bumps are evanescent: as they appear in one area they fade from another, and there may be swelling of the hands, feet, elbows or face [1].

At home, watch for difficulty swallowing or breathing, avoid rubbing the skin or very hot baths, and do not apply powders or ointments or give syrups without asking your paediatrician [3]. A child with hives can eat their usual food without introducing new foods [3].

q: what should I know about malaria symptoms in a child returning from Africa
text: The first symptoms of malaria are usually fever, headache and chills, and they typically appear 10 to 15 days after the bite of an infected mosquito, according to the WHO [2]. Early symptoms can be mild and look like many other febrile illnesses, which makes malaria easy to miss, so testing early matters [2]. In children under 5 the risk of severe infection is higher [2]. Severe signs include extreme tiredness, altered consciousness, seizures, difficulty breathing, dark or bloody urine, yellowing of the eyes and skin, and abnormal bleeding [2]. Anyone with severe symptoms needs emergency care quickly [2]. If your child has fever after travelling to an area where malaria is present, have them tested as soon as possible [2].

q: my child coughs mostly at night but is fine during the day
text:
A cough that is worse at night and fine during the day fits several common childhood conditions, and the pattern alone does not tell them apart. In croup, symptoms generally get worse at night and last three to five days, according to MedlinePlus [6]. In whooping cough, the coughing fits also get worse and happen more often at night, and can last up to 10 weeks or more [2]. Asthma causes wheezing, cough and chest tightness, and is harder to diagnose in small children because it looks like other childhood conditions [5][3].

q: my daughter fainted for a few seconds at school and feels fine now
text:
A fainting spell is a brief, sudden loss of consciousness, and children usually recover quickly after a short rest, according to the SEUP [2][5]. It often happens when not enough blood or oxygen reaches the brain, and common triggers include heat, pain, fear, anxiety, standing still for a long time, or getting up suddenly [2]. Before fainting, a child may feel nauseous, see blurry, have belly pain, sweat, or hear ringing — knowing these signs can help her sit or lie down next time [1][5].

See a doctor if the fainting happened during exercise or while sitting, if it came with palpitations, chest pain, jerking of the limbs, or wetting herself, or if she took more than 3–5 minutes to come round [6].

q: mi hijo tiene fiebre despues de las vacunas
text:
Si el bebé tiene menos de 3 meses, la fiebre necesita que lo vea un médico ese mismo día.

En un niño mayor, la fiebre después de las vacunas es una reacción esperable y suele ser pasajera: los lactantes que fueron prematuros de menos de 28 semanas y pesaron menos de 1500 g tienen más riesgo de apnea y bradicardia en las 48-72 horas siguientes a la vacunación, pero son fenómenos transitorios, según la AEP [3]. La inmunogenicidad y la seguridad de las vacunas sistemáticas son, en general, similares a las de los recién nacidos a término [3]. La dosis de antitérmico depende de la edad y el peso, así que consúltala con su pediatra.

Las edades y dosis de las vacunas siguen el calendario nacional de Estados Unidos, no el de otro país.

Consulta a tu médico si la fiebre es alta o dura más de lo esperado, o si el niño está decaído o con mal aspecto.

q: my 18 month old has a fever of 103 and won't take Tylenol
text:
103 °F = 39.4 °C.

A fever is usually a sign the body is fighting an infection, and most children's temperatures return to normal within 1 to 4 days, according to the NHS [5]. The goal of treatment is your child's comfort, not bringing the number itself down [3].

Acetaminophen (Tylenol) and ibuprofen (Advil, Motrin) both help reduce fever in children [4]. If your child refuses Tylenol, you can offer ibuprofen instead — it is given every 6 to 8 hours, and is not used in children under 6 months [4]. Never give aspirin to a child unless their provider says it is OK [4].

Keep offering plenty of liquids, since it is normal for a child with a fever to have no appetite — do not force them to eat [3]. See your doctor if the fever lasts more than a few days, or if your child seems very unwell, is not drinking, or has a seizure [5].

q: why does my 3 year old have a temperature of 105 degree celsius
text:
105 °F = 40.6 °C.

A temperature of 105 °C is not possible in a living child — that reading is almost certainly a mistake, either in the unit or in the thermometer. Fever is a body temperature above normal, and it is not an illness: it is usually a sign that the body is fighting an infection, according to MedlinePlus [1]. Most fevers are harmless and self-limiting, and fever rarely goes above 40.5 °C (104.9 °F), according to the AEPap [5]. If the thermometer shows a number that seems impossible, check it again and take the temperature in the armpit with a digital thermometer [5]. See a doctor if your child is very sleepy, confused, irritable, behaving unusually, or has a severe headache or repeated vomiting [6].

q: my 5 year old won't stop itching her arms and legs at night
text:
Itching that is worse at night is a classic sign of scabies, according to the WHO [2]. Scabies is an itchy rash caused by mites, spread by close skin contact, and it should be treated quickly to stop it spreading [5]. The itch usually starts 4 to 6 weeks after infestation, and the rash can appear as itchy lines and bumps on the fingers, wrists, arms and legs [2].

See your doctor, because many other things can also cause itchy skin and rashes in children [5].

q: my 14 year old says her throat hurts really bad when swallowing
text:
A sore throat that hurts when swallowing is very common and usually nothing to worry about — it normally gets better by itself within a week, according to the NHS [5]. Most sore throats are caused by viruses like a cold or flu, and only occasionally by bacteria [4]. Tonsillitis is another common cause in teenagers, with red, swollen tonsils and pain on swallowing [2].

To help soothe it: drink plenty of water, eat cool or soft foods, suck ice cubes or ice lollies, and rest [5]. She can also gargle with warm, salty water — half a teaspoon of salt in a glass of warm water, then spit it out [5].

See a doctor if she has a high temperature, swollen painful glands in her neck, white patches on her tonsils, or if it is not improving [2].

q: he has an inhaler but I dont know when to use it
text:
A reliever inhaler with salbutamol is used when there is wheezing, cough or difficulty breathing, because it opens the airways and eases the symptoms, according to the SEUP [2][6]. It should always be given with a spacer, never straight into the mouth, as it works less well otherwise [1]. The most common trigger in young children is a cold, and episodes sometimes start with just a cough [1]. Most of these episodes are mild and can be treated at home, with symptoms settling in a few days, though they can last up to a week [4].

See a doctor if he is very agitated or drowsy, turns blue or pale, breathes faster and faster with his ribs or chest pulling in, or needs the inhaler every two hours or less [1].

q: my 9 month old still has no teeth, is that normal
text: It is normal for a 9-month-old not to have teeth yet: first teeth usually appear between 4 and 8 months, but this varies, according to MedlinePlus [4]. Even before teeth come through, wipe the gums with a damp washcloth after each meal, and start using a soft toothbrush as soon as the first tooth shows [4]. Avoid putting your baby to bed with a bottle of milk, juice or sugar water — use only water for bedtime bottles [4]. Ask your health care provider whether your baby needs oral fluoride [4].

q: she bumped her forehead on the table and cried right away, do I need to watch her
text:
Yes, she should be watched: after a head knock it is important to keep an eye on the child for the first 24 hours to spot signs of something more serious, according to the SEUP [4]. Most head injuries in children are mild and not dangerous, and most recover quickly [4][5]. Let her sleep if she wants to, though after a bigger knock it is worth waking her every 4 hours [5]. She can eat and drink as usual, and if she has a headache you can give paracetamol or ibuprofen at the dose your doctor indicates [5].

See a doctor if she has a severe or worsening headache, repeated vomiting, confusion or unusual irritability, is hard to wake, has trouble speaking or walking, or blood or clear fluid comes from her nose or ears [2].

q: is the MMR vaccine safe for my baby I read online it causes autism
text:
No, the MMR vaccine does not cause autism — studies have found no evidence of a link between the MMR vaccine and autism, according to the NHS [1]. Many scientific studies have looked at this and found no link between vaccines and autism, according to MedlinePlus [5]. The benefits of vaccines far outweigh their risks, and the American Academy of Pediatrics, the National Academy of Medicine and the CDC have all concluded this [3].

Children need 2 doses of MMR vaccine, usually the first at age 12 through 15 months and the second at age 4 through 6 years, following the United States national schedule [6]. Your health care provider can tell you the right time for your baby.

q: she has a fever and cold hands and feet, is that normal
banner: 🚨 With these symptoms your child should be seen in the emergency department today, without waiting. | Reason: Cold hands and feet in a child with fever: it may be poor circulation, get it checked
text:
If your child is under 3 months old, a fever needs a doctor the same day.

Cold hands and feet can be a sign of meningitis, which can be very serious if not treated quickly, according to the NHS [7]. Other signs to look for include a stiff neck, a rash that does not fade when pressed with a glass, being very sleepy or difficult to wake, and a high temperature [7]. While you are on your way, keep them comfortable and do not undress them or sponge them down to cool them, and do not cover them in too many clothes or bedclothes [2].

text: Fewer wet diapers than usual is one of the signs of dehydration in a baby, according to the NHS [4]. Other signs to look for are a sunken soft spot on the head, sunken eyes, few or no tears when they cry, and being drowsy or irritable [4]. In infants and young children, dehydration can also cause a dry mouth and tongue, a high fever, and unusual sleepiness [6]. Keep offering fluids, and if your baby has diarrhoea or vomiting, oral rehydration solution is what replaces the losses [7]. See your doctor if your baby is not wetting diapers for 3 hours or more, is drowsy or irritable, or will not drink [6][7].

He can sleep, but after a more significant knock it is worth waking him every 4 hours [6]. If he has a headache, you can give paracetamol or ibuprofen at the dose your doctor indicates [6].

Hives are raised, red, very itchy patches that move around — they appear in one area and fade from another, according to the SEUP [1]. q: she feels hot but the thermometer says 98.6
text:
A normal temperature is usually around 98.6°F, and it can vary from child to child, according to MedlinePlus [4]. A high temperature is 38°C (100.4°F) or more, and children with one may feel hotter than usual to the touch, feel sweaty, or look unwell, according to the NHS [2]. If she has just had a bath or been wrapped in a blanket, her temperature may read higher for a short time — wait a few minutes and try again [2]. What matters most is how she seems in herself: treat her discomfort, not the number, and make sure she drinks plenty of fluids, according to the SEUP [1]. See a doctor if she has a seizure, or if she seems worse or has a poor colour [2][5].

q: my child has a rash after having a fever, could it be from the fever
text:
If your child is under 3 months old, a fever needs a doctor the same day. For an older child, a rash that appears just as the fever drops is a recognised pattern: a high fever for 3 to 4 days with no other symptoms, then the fever falls and a faint, flat, widespread rash appears that is not itchy and lasts about 48 hours, according to the SEUP [2]. This is called exantema súbito and it is most common between 6 and 18 months, with the diagnosis made from that sequence of events [2]. It is caused by a virus and there is no vaccine for it [2]. See a doctor if your child is floppy or very irritable, has trouble breathing, has spots that do not fade when you press them, or will not take fluids [1].

q: what are the side effects of chickenpox shot
text:
Most side effects of the chickenpox vaccine are mild and do not last long, according to the NHS [1]. They can include swelling or pain where the injection was given, a high temperature, and a rash at the injection site or more widespread, usually within a month of vaccination [1]. More serious side effects, such as a severe allergic reaction, are very rare, and the person who vaccinates your child is trained to treat them immediately [1].

In the United States, the ages and doses for this vaccine follow the US national schedule, so ask your doctor when it is due.

q: my baby has a cough and sounds very congested when sleeping
text:
A blocked nose in a small baby is helped by keeping the nose clear: frequent nasal washes with saline solution ease the obstruction and, in very small infants, prevent breathing difficulty, according to the PUC Chile manual [3]. Treatment is mainly aimed at relieving symptoms, since the illness improves on its own, and honey is among the measures recommended for cough [3]. Do not use cough medicines, decongestants or antihistamines: they have little effect and can cause side effects such as agitation, arrhythmias and apnoea, and the FDA advises avoiding them under 2 years, ideally up to 4 [3].

See a doctor if your baby has severe breathing problems, or if the skin, lips or nails look pale or bluish [1].

q: my 10 month old is pulling his ear and crying a lot
text:
Ear infections are a common cause of ear pulling and crying in babies, and often clear up on their own [1]. In a 10-month-old, pulling at the ear, crying more than usual and trouble sleeping are signs to look for, according to MedlinePlus [1]. Many ear infections get better within about 3 days, though symptoms can sometimes last up to a week [3]. Pain relief can help; ask your doctor what is right for your baby [1].

See your doctor if your baby has a high temperature, fluid draining from the ear, or is not feeding or settling [3].

q: my 3 year old keeps vomiting every time he drinks water

Small sips of water or sucking on ice chips can help when a child is having trouble keeping liquids down, according to MedlinePlus [1]. Offer fluids in small amounts more often than usual, and regular small sips of rehydration solution to replace lost fluids — your pharmacist can recommend one [3]. q: my toddler has very hard poop and cries when he goes
text: Hard poop that hurts to pass is common and usually not serious, according to MedlinePlus [3]. Constipation means fewer than three bowel movements a week, with stool that can be hard and dry and sometimes painful to pass [3]. The main thing is to offer more fluids, preferably water, and more foods with fibre — cereals and wholegrain bread, fruit and vegetables — and not to replace fruit with juice, which has little fibre, according to the SEUP [1]. Most cases of constipation in children are not caused by any illness [1]. See your doctor if there is blood in the stool, severe tummy pain, or repeated vomiting [1].

Growth spurts, teething and illnesses can all affect how your baby sleeps [2]. If your baby is feeding normally when they wake, that fits with a baby who is simply sleeping more than usual [1]. If you are worried about their sleep or want advice on routines, speak to your pediatrician [2].

q: my baby has been vomiting for six hours but still wants to breastfeed
text:
Keep breastfeeding — offer it normally, and even more often if your baby wants it [1]. Give smaller amounts more frequently rather than a long break, and do not stop feeding to "rest the stomach" [1]. Vomiting usually settles on its own within less than a week, according to the SEUP [3].

See a doctor if your baby is under 3 months and has vomited two or more feeds, is drowsy or floppy, has sunken eyes, cries without tears, is very thirsty or is passing little urine [4]. Also seek care if the vomit is green, contains blood, or looks like coffee grounds [4].

text: बच्चे का वज़न कितना है? पैरासिटामोल की खुराक उम्र से नहीं, वज़न से तय होती है: वज़न बताइए, फिर सही मात्रा बताई जाएगी।

q: मेरे बच्चे को कल से दस्त हो रहे हैं और वह खाना नहीं खा रहा
banner: 💛 यह ज़रूरी है और आप अकेले नहीं हैं। Tele-MANAS 14416 पर कॉल करें (या 112 पर अगर खतरा अभी है)। अगर बच्चे ने खुद को नुकसान पहुँचाया है, तो अभी इमरजेंसी ले जाएँ। | कारण: खानपान के विकार के संकेत
text: दस्त में खाना बंद करने की ज़रूरत नहीं है — बच्चे को लगभग सामान्य खाना जारी रखना चाहिए, बस थोड़ी-थोड़ी मात्रा में और बार-बार, बच्चे की भूख का सम्मान करते हुए, सेव के अनुसार [6]। विश्व स्वास्थ्य संगठन के अनुसार दस्त का इलाज ओरल रीहाइड्रेशन सॉल्ट (ORS) से किया जाता है, और साथ ही ज़िंक की गोलियाँ दी जाती हैं, जो दस्त की अवधि कम करती हैं [4]। ज़िंक की खुराक और कितने दिन देनी है, यह डॉक्टर तय करेंगे। बच्चे को दूध पिलाना जारी रखें, और ज़्यादा मांगे तो और बार [6]। अगर बच्चा बहुत उल्टी करे, तरल भी न रख पाए, या उल्टी में हरा रंग, खून या कॉफ़ी जैसा भूरा पदार्थ हो, तो डॉक्टर से मिलें [6]।

q: मेरे बच्चे को बुखार के साथ लाल दाने निकल आए हैं
text:
अगर बच्चा 3 महीने से छोटा है, तो बुखार में उसी दिन डॉक्टर को दिखाना ज़रूरी है।

बुखार के साथ लाल दाने कई बीमारियों में हो सकते हैं। हैंड, फुट एंड माउथ डिज़ीज़ में पहले गले में दर्द, तेज़ बुखार और खाने का मन न करना होता है, और कुछ दिन बाद मुँह के छाले तथा हाथ-पैरों पर उभरे हुए लाल दाने निकलते हैं, जो फफोले बन सकते हैं — यह NHS के अनुसार है [3]। यह आमतौर पर 7 से 10 दिन में खुद ठीक हो जाता है और इसका कोई दवा से इलाज नहीं है [1]। खसरे में दाने पहले लक्षणों के 3 से 5 दिन बाद चेहरे पर बालों की लाइन से शुरू होकर नीचे की ओर फैलते हैं, और दाने निकलते समय बुखार तेज़ हो सकता है — यह CDC के अनुसार है [4]। चिकनपॉक्स में खुजली वाले दाने शरीर पर कहीं भी हो सकते हैं, और उससे पहले या बाद में तेज़ बुखार हो सकता है [5]।

दवा की खुराक बच्चे की उम्र और वज़न पर निर्भर करती है, इसलिए अपने डॉक्टर से पूछें। अगर दाने के साथ मुँह के आसपास सूजन हो या बच्चे को साँस लेने में तकलीफ़ हो, तो तुरंत मदद लें [6]।

बच्चे की उम्र कितनी है? उम्र जानकर मैं जवाब और सटीक कर सकता हूँ।

q: मेरा 6 महीने का बच्चा दूध कम पी रहा है और पेशाब भी कम कर रहा है
banner: 🚨 इन लक्षणों के साथ बच्चे को आज ही इमरजेंसी में दिखाना चाहिए, देर न करें। | कारण: पानी की कमी के लक्षण: आँखें धँसी, कम पेशाब, सूखा मुँह, लगातार उल्टी या 24 घंटे से ज़्यादा दस्त
text:
नमस्ते। आपके बच्चे की स्थिति को लेकर आपकी चिंता बिल्कुल जायज़ है।

चूँकि बच्चा दूध और पेशाब दोनों कम कर रहा है, इसलिए सबसे ज़रूरी है कि उसे तरल पदार्थ दिए जाते रहें। SEUP के अनुसार, बच्चे को भूखा नहीं रखना चाहिए और स्तनपान सामान्य रूप से, बल्कि बच्चे की माँग पर और भी अधिक बार कराना चाहिए [1]। अगर बच्चा ठोस आहार लेता है, तो उसे थोड़ी-थोड़ी मात्रा में और बार-बार देना चाहिए ताकि उल्टी का ख़तरा कम हो [1]।

अगर बच्चा बहुत ज़्यादा उल्टी करता है, ठोस या तरल कुछ भी नहीं पचा पाता, या बिना कुछ पिए भी उल्टी करता है, तो तुरंत डॉक्टर से मिलें [1]।

q: मेरी बेटी बिस्तर से गिर गई और उसके बाद एक बार उल्टी हुई
banner: 🚨 इन लक्षणों के साथ बच्चे को आज ही इमरजेंसी में दिखाना चाहिए, देर न करें। | कारण: सिर पर चोट के बाद उल्टी
text: सिर की चोट के बाद उल्टी होने पर डॉक्टर को दिखाना ज़रूरी है, और रास्ते में बच्चे को अपने पास रखें और होश में रहने पर नज़र रखें [1]। SEUP के अनुसार, अगर बच्चा तीन महीने से छोटा है, या गिरावट एक मीटर से ज़्यादा ऊँचाई से हुई है, तो भी तुरंत डॉक्टर के पास जाना चाहिए [1]। डॉक्टर ज़रूरी जाँच करेंगे और तय करेंगे कि कोई अतिरिक्त टेस्ट चाहिए या नहीं, हालाँकि ज़्यादातर मामलों में इसकी ज़रूरत नहीं पड़ती [1]। अगर बच्चे का व्यवहार या हालत आपको चिंताजनक लगे, तो भी डॉक्टर को दिखाएँ [1]।

q: बच्चे को कब्ज है और पॉटी करते समय बहुत रोता है
text: कब्ज से बच्चे का रोना हो सकता है — NHS के अनुसार रोने के कारणों में कब्ज भी शामिल है [2]। अगर बच्चा लगातार रो रहा है और आप उसे शांत या ध्यान भटका नहीं पा रहे हैं, या रोना उसके सामान्य रोने जैसा नहीं लग रहा, तो यह बीमारी का संकेत हो सकता है [4]। ऐसे में डॉक्टर से मिलें या अपने इलाके के आपातकालीन नंबर पर कॉल करें, खासकर अगर तेज़ बुखार हो या बच्चा दूध पीने में रुचि न ले रहा हो [4]। अगर रोने के बीच बच्चा सामान्य न हो, रोने के साथ पीलापन, पसीना, सुस्ती या दूध न लेना हो, या बुखार, उल्टी या खून वाली पॉटी हो, तो तुरंत डॉक्टर से मिलें [6]।

q: मेरे बच्चे के हाथ पैर ठंडे हैं लेकिन शरीर गर्म है
text: जब बुखार चढ़ रहा होता है तो बच्चे का ठंड लगना, कंपकंपी आना और हाथ-पैर ठंडे होना सामान्य है, और त्वचा पर जाल जैसा धब्बेदार रूप भी दिख सकता है, खासकर हाथों और पैरों पर — यह SEUP के अनुसार होता है [2]। जब बुखार उतरता है तो बच्चा पसीना-पसीना हो जाता है, लाल पड़ जाता है और उसे गर्मी लगती है [2]। बुखार का मतलब यह है कि शरीर किसी संक्रमण से लड़ रहा है, और यह अपने आप में गंभीरता का संकेत नहीं है [4]। बुखार में भूख कम लगना, थकान या सिरदर्द भी सामान्य है [2]। अगर बच्चा सुस्त पड़ जाए, उसे उठाया-बिठाया न जा सके, या बुखार के साथ कोई और चिंता की बात दिखे, तो डॉक्टर से मिलें [4]।

q: मेरे बच्चे ने आज बहुत कम पेशाब किया है
banner: 🚨 इन लक्षणों के साथ बच्चे को आज ही इमरजेंसी में दिखाना चाहिए, देर न करें। | कारण: पानी की कमी के लक्षण: आँखें धँसी, कम पेशाब, सूखा मुँह, लगातार उल्टी या 24 घंटे से ज़्यादा दस्त
text:
नमस्ते। बच्चे का कम पेशाब करना निर्जलीकरण का संकेत हो सकता है, और ऊपर दिए गए निर्देश के अनुसार आज ही डॉक्टर से मिलना ज़रूरी है।

तब तक, SEUP के अनुसार बच्चे को भूखा न रखें — सामान्य भोजन जारी रखें, बस थोड़ी-थोड़ी मात्रा में और बार-बार, ताकि उल्टी का ख़तरा कम हो [1]। स्तनपान सामान्य रूप से, और अगर बच्चा माँगे तो और भी बार-बार कराएँ [1]। चिकनी चीज़ें, मिठाइयाँ और जूस से बचें; खेल-पेय (sports drinks) भी न दें क्योंकि उनमें शक्कर बहुत ज़्यादा और इलेक्ट्रोलाइट असंतुलित होते हैं [1]।

अगर बच्चा बहुत उल्टी करे, तरल भी न रख पाए, या उल्टी हरी, ख़ून वाली या कॉफ़ी जैसी भूरी हो, तो तुरंत आपातकालीन विभाग जाएँ [1]।

q: मेरी बेटी को तेज बुखार और बैंगनी जैसे दाग हो गए हैं
banner: 🚨 अभी 112 पर कॉल करें या तुरंत इमरजेंसी ले जाएँ। | कारण: दबाने पर न मिटने वाले दाने (सेप्सिस या मेनिन्जाइटिस का शक)
text:
अगर बच्चा 3 महीने से छोटा है, तो बुखार में उसी दिन डॉक्टर को दिखाना ज़रूरी है।

बुखार शरीर की संक्रमण से लड़ने की स्वाभाविक प्रतिक्रिया है, और आमतौर पर 1 से 4 दिनों में तापमान सामान्य हो जाता है [3]। त्वचा पर ऐसे दाग जो दबाने पर भी न मिटें, तुरंत ध्यान देने वाला लक्षण हैं [1]। बच्चे को ठंडा करने के लिए कपड़े न उतारें और न स्पंज करें, और ज़्यादा कपड़ों या रज़ाई में न लपेटें [2]। 16 साल से कम उम्र के बच्चे को एस्पिरिन न दें [2]। दवा की मात्रा बच्चे की उम्र और वज़न पर निर्भर करती है, इसलिए डॉक्टर जो बताएँ वही दें।

रास्ते में बच्चे को आराम से रखें और उसका ध्यान रखें।

q: mere 3 saal ke bacche ko bukhar 102 hai, paracetamol kitna du
text: Paracetamol bukhar aur dard kam karne mein madad karta hai, aur ise har 4 se 6 ghante mein diya ja sakta hai, AEPap ke mutabiq [3]. Din mein paanch se zyada baar nahi dena chahiye, kyunki zyada dene se liver ko nuksan ho sakta hai [3]. Sahi khurak bachche ke wazan se nikalti hai, umar se nahi [3]. PediBot ka dose calculator paracetamol ke liye maujood hai — usme wazan daal kar sahi miqdar dekh lein. Agar 3-4 ghante baad bhi bukhar tez hai aur bachcha bechain hai, to paracetamol ki jagah ibuprofen diya ja sakta hai [5].
sources: [3] AEPap — "Antitérmicos (para la fiebre)", section "¿Cuándo utilizar los antitérmicos?",
[5] AEPap — "Antitérmicos (para la fiebre)", section "¿Cuándo utilizar los antitérmicos?",

q: mera baby raat ko bahut khans raha hai
text:
Raat ko khansi hona asthma ka ek aam lakshan hai. MedlinePlus ke mutabik bachchon mein asthma ke symptoms mein khansi shaamil hai, khaaskar raat ko ya subah jaldi [3]. SEUP bhi kehta hai ki bachchon mein khansi ho sakti hai, kabhi kabhi raat ko [2].

Dhyaan dene wali baatein: saans lene mein takleef ya tez saans, seene ka dhadakna, hothon ke aas paas neela rang, ya doodh peene mein dikkat [2][3]. Aise lakshan dikhein to turant doctor se milna chahiye [3].

util.note: La respuesta se centra solo en asma y no ofrece causas comunes ni medidas caseras para la tos nocturna en un bebé.

q: mere bete ke pairon par lal dane hain aur khujli ho rahi hai
text: Aapke bete ke pairon par lal dane aur khujli heat rash (prickly heat) ke lakshan ho sakte hain — chhote, ubhre hue dane aur khujli wali feeling iske aam lakshan hain, NHS ke mutabik [4]. Heat rash aam taur par kuch dinon mein khud theek ho jata hai [6]. Ise thanda rakhna sabse zaroori hai: dheele cotton kapde pehnaayein, halki rajai use karein, aur thande paani se nahiyein [4]. Khujli kam karne ke liye thandi cheez (geela kapda ya ice pack, towel mein lipta hua) 20 minute tak lagayein, aur khujaane ki jagah dane par thap thap karein [4]. Perfume wale shower gel ya cream use na karein [4]. Agar aap sure nahi hain ki ye heat rash hai, to doctor se milna behtar hai [6].

text: Kabz mein potty karte waqt bachche ka dard aur rona ho sakta hai, aur yeh kabz ka ek jaana-maana lakshan hai [3]. Kabz ke saath rone ke baare mein zyada jaankari ke liye apne doctor se baat karein [3].

banner: 🚨 अभी 112 पर कॉल करें या तुरंत इमरजेंसी ले जाएँ। | कारण: साँस लेने में गंभीर दिक्कत (पसलियाँ दिखना, बहुत तेज़ साँस, साँस रुकना, नीलापन)

Bronchiolitis mein bachche ki saans tez ho jaati hai, wheezing ya crackling awaaz aati hai, aur doodh peena kam ho jaata hai [5]. q: meri beti bahut sust hai aur jag nahi rahi
banner: 🚨 इन लक्षणों के साथ बच्चे को आज ही इमरजेंसी में दिखाना चाहिए, देर न करें। | कारण: बहुत ज़्यादा सुस्ती या चिड़चिड़ापन
text:
Sust hona aur jag nahi pana bachchon mein ek gambhir lakshan ho sakta hai. WHO ke mutabik sepsis ek medical emergency hai, aur bachchon mein sust hona ya jag nahi pana iske lakshan ho sakte hain [4]. SEUP ke mutabik somnolencia ya bachche ko jagane mein mushkil hona turant urgences mein dikhane ka sanket hai [5]. Canada ki sarkar bhi kehti hai ki agar bachcha jag nahi raha ya logon se interact nahi kar raha to turant health care provider se baat karein [7].

Agar bachche ko saans lene mein dikkat, daure, ya twacha ka pale hona dikhe to ye bhi sepsis ke lakshan hain [4].

q: my 2 year old has bad cough at night not sleeping
text:
A cough that is worse at night is one of the signs of whooping cough, according to the NHS: after about a week of cold-like symptoms, children get coughing bouts that last for a few minutes and are worse at night [2]. The coughing fits get worse and happen more often, especially at night, and can last up to 10 weeks or more [3]. Croup is another cause of a night cough — a barking cough that sounds like a seal, often worse at night [5].

See a doctor if the cough is very bad and getting worse, or if your child's lips, tongue, face or skin turn blue or grey, or they are finding it hard to breathe [4].

q: my 5 year old baby has red pimples on full body
text: A rash that spreads over the whole body can be caused by several different illnesses, and the pattern matters. In measles, the rash usually starts on the face and upper neck and moves down over about three days to the torso, arms, legs and feet, along with fever, runny nose, cough and red watery eyes, according to the WHO [4]. Chickenpox causes an itchy rash that turns into fluid-filled blisters and then scabs, often starting on the face, chest and back before spreading, according to MedlinePlus [5]. Measles can lead to serious complications, especially in children under five, so it is worth having your child seen [4].

q: my 6 year old child is not eating anything from 2 days
text: A child who refuses to eat or drink should be seen, according to the SEUP [1]. The most important thing is to prevent dehydration with oral rehydration solutions that come already prepared; homemade solutions and commercial soft drinks should not be used [1]. If your child is very thirsty, cries without tears, urinates little or has sunken eyes, they need to be checked [1]. Offer food in smaller amounts and more often, respecting their appetite, and do not force a fast [2]. See a doctor if the refusal to eat or drink continues, or if there is marked irritability, drowsiness or less responsiveness [1].

q: my 6 month old baby has congested chest and making whistling noise
banner: 🚨 With these symptoms your child should be seen in the emergency department today, without waiting. | Reason: Breathing difficulty: fast breathing, wheezing, ribs pulling in
text: A whistling or wheezing noise with a congested chest in a 6-month-old is often caused by a viral respiratory infection, and in preschool children viral infections are the main cause of wheezing, according to the SEUP [2]. Bronchiolitis is one such infection: it usually starts like a normal cold with cough and mucus, and after 2 to 4 days breathing difficulty can appear, with fast breathing, irritability and trouble feeding [4]. Wheezing is more common in viral infections, according to the WHO [5]. Keep feeding them and watch their breathing while you travel to be seen.

q: क्या बुखार उतारने के लिए बच्चे को नहला सकती हूँ? (उम्र: 6 महीने) (वज़न: 5 किलो)
text:
नहीं, बुखार उतारने के लिए बच्चे को नहलाने के बजाय गुनगुने पानी में कपड़ा भिगोकर पूरे शरीर को पोंछना चाहिए — सिर्फ माथा नहीं, पूरा शरीर, ऐसा विकासपीडिया कहता है [3]। बुखार आमतौर पर 1 से 4 दिनों में अपने आप सामान्य हो जाता है, और 38°C या उससे ज़्यादा तापमान को बुखार माना जाता है, ऐसा NHS बताता है [1]। अगर बच्चे ने अभी नहाया हो या कंबल में लपेटा गया हो, तो तापमान कुछ देर के लिए ज़्यादा दिख सकता है — कुछ मिनट रुककर फिर नापें [1]।

डॉक्टर से तुरंत मिलें अगर बुखार से दौरे पड़ें, बच्चा खाने-पीने या स्तनपान से मना कर दे, सुस्त हो जाए, साँस लेते समय पसलियाँ अंदर खिंचें, या त्वचा, होंठ या नाखूनों पर नीली झलक दिखे [3]।

ध्यान दें: WHO के विकास चार्ट के अनुसार 6 महीने के बच्चे के लिए 5 किग्रा बहुत कम वज़न है। अगर वज़न सही है तो जल्द ही डॉक्टर से बच्चे की बढ़त जँचवाएँ; अगर लिखने में गलती हुई है तो उसे ठीक करें, क्योंकि दवा की खुराक वज़न से तय होती है।

q: मेरे 5 साल के बच्चे के शरीर पर लाल दाने हो गए हैं और खुजली है
text:
लाल दाने और खुजली स्केबीज़ (खाज) के कारण हो सकते हैं — यह छोटे परजीवी कीड़ों से होता है जो त्वचा में घुसकर अंडे देते हैं और तेज़ खुजली व दाने पैदा करते हैं [2]। उंगलियों के बीच अक्सर उभरी हुई लकीरें दिखती हैं जिनके एक सिरे पर बिंदु होता है, और स्केबीज़ का इलाज आमतौर पर घर पर ही किया जा सकता है [4]। यह त्वचा से त्वचा के संपर्क से फैलता है और किसी की भी हो सकता है — इसका गंदगी या सफ़ाई से कोई संबंध नहीं है [1]। इलाज के लिए क्रीम या मुँह से ली जाने वाली दवा दी जाती है [2]।

डॉक्टर से मिलें अगर:
- बच्चा 2 साल से छोटा हो और स्केबीज़ के लक्षण हों, या घर में किसी और को भी स्केबीज़ हो [1]
- त्वचा में संक्रमण लगने का लगे, या खुजली इलाज खत्म होने के 2 से 4 हफ़्ते बाद भी बनी रहे [1]

q: क्या एमएमआर वैक्सीन बच्चे के लिए सुरक्षित है
text:
हाँ, टीके सुरक्षित हैं। विकासपीडिया के अनुसार लगभग सभी वैक्सीन्स के हल्के दुष्प्रभाव हो सकते हैं, पर ये सारे टीके काफी सुरक्षित हैं और दुष्प्रभावों का मामूली उपचार से इलाज हो जाता है [6]। दुष्प्रभाव होना यह संकेत है कि वैक्सीन असर दिखा रही है [6]। nidirect के अनुसार टीके सुरक्षित और प्रभावी हैं तथा गंभीर बीमारियों से बचाते हैं [4]।

भारत में एमएमआर सहित टीकों की उम्र और खुराक राष्ट्रीय टीकाकरण कार्यक्रम के अनुसार तय होती है, इसलिए अपने बच्चे के टीकाकरण की जानकारी अपने डॉक्टर से लें [4]।

[6] Vikaspedia — "वैक्सीन्स की प्रभावशीलता, सुरक्षा तथा दुष्प्रभाव — स्रोत: वालेंटरी हेल्थ

q: 3 saal ke bacche ko raat ko bahut khansi aati hai
text:
Raat ki khansi asthma ke lakshan ho sakti hai: MedlinePlus ke mutabik bachchon mein asthma se khaas taur par raat ko ya subah jaldi khansi hoti hai [5]. SEUP bhi kehta hai ki asthma mein khansi raat ko ho sakti hai, saath hi saans phoolna aur seeti jaisi awaaz sunai de sakti hai [1].

Dhyan rakhein agar saans lene mein dikkat, tez saans, ya honth neele pad jayein — turant doctor se milna zaroori hai [5].

- Saans lene mein problem ya tez saans [4]
- Bukhar 4 din se zyada [4]
- Lakshan 10 din se zyada bina sudhar [4]
sources: [1] SEUP — "Crisis asmática. Información para padres" (2025), section "¿CUÁLES SON LOS SÍN
[4] MedlinePlus — "Resfrío", section "¿Cuáles son los tratamientos para el resfrío común?"
[5] MedlinePlus — "Asma en niños", section "¿Cuáles son los síntomas del asma en los niños

signs of breathing difficulty in a child: chest indrawing, ribs showing, nostrils flaring, unable to speak or feed

q: mera 8 month ka baby bed se gir gaya aur ro raha hai
text:
Bed se girne ke baad bachche ko aaram chahiye: SEUP ke mutabik 24 se 48 ghante tak sharirik aur mansik aaram zaroori hai, aur is dauran khel-kood aur mobile, tablet ya video games se door rakhna chahiye [2]. Agar sar dard ho to doctor ki batayi hui khurak mein ibuprofen ya paracetamol di ja sakti hai [6]. Pehle 24 ghante dhyan se nazar rakhein [3].

Doctor se turant milein agar:

- Baar-baar ulti ho, ya bachcha bahut chidchida ho ya jagane par mushkil se jaage [2]
- Naak ya kaan se khoon ya saaf paani nikle [2]
- Chalne ya bolne mein dikkat ho, ya behaviour badal jaye [2]
- Girne ki unchai ek meter se zyada thi [5]

q: 5 saal ke child ko body pe red rashes ho gaye hain
text:
5 saal ke bachche ki body par red rashes ke kai aam karan ho sakte hain. MedlinePlus ke mutabik eccema (dermatitis) se skin sookhi ho jaati hai, khujli hoti hai aur chehre, kohni ke andar, ghutnon ke peeche, haath aur pairon par sarpulli nikal aati hai; ye chhune se nahi failta [6]. WHO ke mutabik sarna (scabies) mein tez khujli hoti hai, khaas kar raat mein, aur ungliyon, kalai, baahon, pairon aur kamar ke aas-paas dane aur lines ban jaati hain [2]. WHO ke mutabik khasra (measles) mein tez bukhar, khansi, naak behna aur aankhein laal hone ke 3-5 din baad rash nikalta hai, jo chehre se shuru hokar neeche poore sharir par failta hai [3].

Doctor se milein agar:
- Bukhar ke saath rash ho [3]
- Saans lene mein dikkat ya sust ho [3]
- Rash tez fail raha ho ya khujli bahut zyada ho [2]
sources: [2] WHO — "Sarna", section "Síntomas", p. 1 — https://www.who.int/es/news-room/fact-sheets
[3] WHO — "Sarampión", section "Signos y síntomas", p. 1 — https://www.who.int/es/news-roo
[6] MedlinePlus — "Eccema", p. 1 — https://medlineplus.gov/spanish/eczema.html

missing: common causes of red rash in a child: viral exanthem, heat rash, allergic reaction, chickenpox
check for red flags: rash that does not blanch when pressed, neck stiffness, lethargy, dehydration
practical care: keep skin cool, loose cotton clothes, calamine, antihistamine for itching
when to see a doctor urgently vs routine, and how to monitor at home

q: kya polio ki drop dena zaroori hai
text: Polio ki vaccine zaroori hai: poliomielitis ek bahut sankramak viral bimari hai jo pakka paralysis kar sakti hai [4]. Duniya bhar mein 2025 mein lagbhag 86% shishuon ko IPV ki pehli dose mili thi [4]. Polio ke wild virus ab sirf Afghanistan aur Pakistan mein hain, lekin jab tak wahan transmission rukta nahi, doosre deshon mein bhi inke aane ka khatra rehta hai [4]. Isliye vaccination jaari rakhna zaroori hai [4].
sources: [4] WHO — "Cobertura de la inmunización", section "Cobertura vacunal mundial en 2025", p.

util.note: Dice que la vacuna es necesaria, pero no explica el calendario de la India ni dónde poner las gotas gratis.

q: my baby has diarrhea after we came back from a trip
text:
Diarrhoea after a trip is usually an infection picked up from food or water, and it is treated with oral rehydration salts and zinc supplements, according to the WHO [2][4]. Rehydration with ORS replaces the water and electrolytes lost in the stools, and zinc reduces how long the episode lasts by about 25% [2]. Keep giving nutrient-rich foods, including breast milk, during the episode [2]. Hand washing with soap helps stop it spreading to others at home [2].

See a doctor if there is blood in the stool, signs of dehydration, or the diarrhoea lasts 14 days or more [2][4].
sources: [2] WHO — "Diarrhoeal disease", section "Prevention and treatment", p. 1 — https://www.who
[4] WHO — "Enfermedades diarreicas", section "Prevención y tratamiento", p. 1 — https://ww

when to seek care urgently for a young infant (e.g. under 6 months, vomiting, fever, refusing feeds)

q: क्या टीका लगने के बाद बुखार आना सामान्य है?
text:
अगर बच्चा 3 महीने से छोटा है, तो बुखार में उसी दिन डॉक्टर को दिखाना ज़रूरी है।

हाँ, टीके के बाद हल्का बुखार आना सामान्य है और चिंता की बात नहीं है — विकासपीडिया के अनुसार डी.पी.टी. या डी.टी. का इंजेक्शन लगने के कुछ घंटों बाद बच्चे को हल्का बुखार हो सकता है [5]। खसरे के टीके में यह बुखार टीके के 6-7 दिन बाद आ सकता है, साथ में शरीर पर हल्के लाल दाने भी [5]। ये लक्षण आम तौर पर 2-3 दिनों में अपने आप ठीक हो जाते हैं [5]।

डॉक्टर से कब मिलें: अगर लक्षण 2-3 दिनों में ठीक न हों, या इंजेक्शन की जगह लाल, गर्म या सूज जाए, तो स्वास्थ्य कर्मचारी से परामर्श करें [5]। बुखार की दवा की खुराक बच्चे की उम्र और वज़न पर निर्भर करती है, इसलिए टीका लगाने वाले स्वास्थ्य कर्मचारी की सलाह मानें [5]।

बच्चे की उम्र कितनी है? उम्र जानकर मैं जवाब और सटीक कर सकता हूँ।
sources: [5] Vikaspedia — "वैक्सीन्स की प्रभावशीलता, सुरक्षा तथा दुष्प्रभाव — स्रोत: वालेंटरी हेल्थ

q: my child has been in the sun and now feels dizzy
text: Dizziness after being in the sun can be a sign of a heat-related illness, and children are at higher risk [5]. Move your child to a cool, shaded place, take off extra clothing, and apply cool wet cloths to the forehead, neck and armpits, according to the SEUP [6]. Offer cool water in small sips and use a fan to help bring the temperature down [6]. Heat stroke is a life-threatening illness that can raise body temperature above 41°C within minutes, with symptoms including dry skin, fast strong pulse, dizziness, nausea and confusion [5]. If you see any of these signs, get medical help immediately [5].

q: solids baby ko kab se dena shuru kare
text: AEP ke anusar, solids (alimentación complementaria) lagbhag 6 mahine ki umar par shuru karne chahiye [4]. Breastfeeding wale babies ke liye 6 mahine tak intezaar karna recommend kiya jata hai, kyunki 4 se 6 mahine ke beech shuru karne se koi fayda nahi mila aur infection ka khatra badh sakta hai [4]. Kabhi bhi 4 mahine se pehle solids nahi dena chahiye [4][5]. WHO bhi kehti hai ki breastfeeding jaari rakhein aur 6 mahine ke aas-paas, ek-ek karke alag-alag khane shuru karein [6].

q: my child has loose motions since morning what should I give
text:
Give your child an oral rehydration solution to replace the fluids and electrolytes they are losing, according to MedlinePlus [1]. The WHO says these solutions are a mix of clean water, salt and sugar, and that zinc supplements shorten the diarrhoea by about 25% [3]. Keep offering food — there is no need to fast, just give smaller amounts more often, and avoid fatty foods, sweets and juices; sports drinks should be avoided because they have too much sugar for a child with diarrhoea [6]. Do not give any medicine to stop the diarrhoea or vomiting without asking your paediatrician [4].

See a doctor if your child is very thirsty, cries without tears, urinates little or has sunken eyes, is very irritable or drowsy, cannot drink as fast as they are losing fluid, refuses to eat or drink, or has persistent belly pain or stools with a lot of blood [4].

q: is MMR vaccine safe for my daughter
text:
The MMR vaccine is safe and effective. Protection starts within 2 weeks of having it, and after 2 doses around 99% of people are protected against measles and rubella and around 88% against mumps, according to the NHS [2]. If mumps does occur after vaccination, the symptoms are usually much milder [2].

In India, the ages at which MMR is given follow the national immunisation schedule, so check the timing with your doctor.

util.note: Responde que es segura pero no menciona efectos secundarios habituales ni cuándo consultar.

q: my 6 month old has started solids, can I give banana
text: Yes, banana is fine: it is listed among the finger foods you can offer, cut into pieces big enough for your baby to hold in their fist with a bit sticking out, according to the NHS [6]. Soft fruit such as banana, peach or melon works well, and harder fruits like apple and pear should be cooked without adding sugar [6]. Avoid hard foods such as whole nuts or raw carrots and apples, to reduce the risk of choking [6]. At first, how much your baby eats matters less than getting them used to eating, and they still get most of their energy and nutrients from breast milk or first infant formula [4].

q: my 5 year old has stomach pain and constipation
text:
Stomach ache is a common symptom in children and most causes are mild and get better on their own, including constipation and gas, according to the SEUP [2]. Constipation often causes stomach ache and bloating, and it is likely if your child has not pooed at least 3 times in the last week, or the poo is large, dry, hard or lumpy, or they strain or feel pain when they poo [1].

For a 5-year-old, the main things that help are drinking more fluids, preferably water, and eating more fibre — wholegrain cereals and bread, fruit and vegetables — without replacing fruit with juice, which has little fibre [3]. Most cases of childhood constipation are not caused by any disease, and it usually improves with these diet changes [3].

See a doctor if the pain is severe, if your child is very unwell and complaining a lot, if there is blood in the poo, or if they vomit repeatedly and cannot keep down food or fluids [3]. Do not give laxatives or enemas without asking your paediatrician [3].

q: my 3 year old has malaria fever or maybe teething, how can I tell
text:
Malaria's most common early symptoms are fever, headache and chills, according to the WHO [1]. In young children the first symptoms are often mild and hard to recognise as malaria, and without treatment the most dangerous form can become severe within 24 hours [1]. Teething is not covered by the information available here, so it cannot be compared with these symptoms.

If your child has a fever and you are in or have travelled to an area where malaria occurs, have them seen by a doctor the same day.

q: my child has been scratching small bumps on his body
text: Small, itchy raised spots can be heat rash, according to the NHS. Heat rash looks like small, raised spots with an itchy, prickly feeling and mild swelling, and it can appear anywhere on the body and spread [2]. It happens when the skin sweats and gets irritated, so the main thing is to keep the skin cool: loose cotton clothing, lightweight bedding, cool baths, and plenty of fluids [2]. To calm the itching, apply something cold wrapped in a cloth for up to 20 minutes, and pat the rash instead of scratching it [2]. Itchy bumps can also be scabies, which the WHO describes as intense itching that is often worse at night, with bumps and lines on the fingers, wrists, arms, legs and around the waist [5]. See your doctor if the rash is bad, does not go away, or comes with other symptoms [3].

q: my daughter has fever after coming back from a trip
text:
If your child is under 3 months old, a fever needs a doctor the same day. For an older child, fever is very common and the temperature usually returns to normal within 1 to 4 days, according to the NHS [1]. A high temperature is 38C or more, and you can check it with a digital thermometer placed in the top of the armpit [1]. Fever is usually a sign the body is fighting an infection, and most fevers are caused by infections, according to MedlinePlus [3]. Give plenty of fluids to prevent dehydration, and do not give aspirin to a child with fever [3]. Contact your doctor when you return home if your child was sick with a fever while travelling [6].

q: what food to give 6 month baby for first time
text: Around 6 months, milk alone no longer meets a baby's energy and nutrient needs, so solid foods are introduced alongside it, according to the WHO [3]. Start with small amounts and increase them gradually as your baby grows [3]. Offer just a few pieces or teaspoons of food at first, before their usual milk feed, and keep offering different foods even if they are refused — it can take 10 tries or more [2]. Breast milk or first infant formula stays their main drink, and you can offer sips of water from an open cup with meals [2]. Aim for 2–3 meals a day at this age [3].

q: my 1 year old has hot body 39 degree since yesterday
text:
A fever is a body temperature above 38°C, and it is a defence mechanism, not a sign of seriousness by itself, according to the SEUP [2]. Most often it lasts two to four days, and it can last longer without that meaning the child is worse [3]. Fever medicines lower the temperature but do not always bring it down completely, especially when it starts very high, so it staying up after a dose is common and not a sign of greater seriousness [3].

Watch your child's general state and colour, and look for small red spots that do not fade when you press their sides — if you see those, or your child seems worse, see a doctor [3].

q: my 18 month old is refusing food and crying when chewing
text:
Pain when chewing and refusing food can point to a problem in the mouth, such as tooth decay. Tooth decay happens when plaque turns sugars from food and drink into acids that over time destroy the teeth, and it can cause pain and sometimes infection, according to the WHO [2]. See your doctor or dentist if your child keeps refusing food or seems in pain, so the mouth can be checked.

q: my 3 year old has watery stool and weakness
text:
Watery stools with weakness can be gastroenteritis, which is usually not serious, according to MedlinePlus [2]. The weakness matters: it can be a sign of dehydration, so watch for thirst, dry mouth, urinating less than usual or no wet diapers for 3 hours or more, and no tears when crying [2].

Treatment has two key parts, according to the WHO: oral rehydration salts, a mixture of clean water, salt and sugar, and zinc supplements, which shorten the diarrhoea and reduce stool volume [6]. Keep giving nutritious food, including milk, during the episode [6].

See a doctor if the diarrhoea lasts more than a day in a child, if there is any fever, frequent loose stools, vomiting often, severe belly pain, blood or black stools, or signs of dehydration [2].

q: what can I give my 2 year old for diarrhoea
text:
For diarrhoea, the main treatment is oral rehydration salts (ORS) — a mixture of clean water, salt and sugar that replaces the water and electrolytes lost in the stools, according to the WHO [1]. Zinc supplements are also a key measure: they reduce how long the diarrhoea lasts by about 25% and cut stool volume by around 30% [1]. Keep giving nutrient-rich foods, including breast milk, during the episode [1]. Do not use homemade solutions or fizzy drinks to replace the losses, and do not give medicines for diarrhoea or vomiting without asking your paediatrician, according to the SEUP [3].

See a doctor if your child is very thirsty, cries without tears, wees little or has sunken eyes, is very irritable or drowsy, refuses to eat or drink, has persistent or intense tummy pain, or has stools with a lot of blood [3].

In babies and young children, signs of dehydration include a dry mouth and tongue, crying without tears, and not wetting their nappies for 3 hours or more, according to MedlinePlus [5]. Get medical help immediately if there is no passing of urine, confusion, fainting, fast heartbeat or fast breathing [5].

q: my baby fell from the bed and seems normal now
text:
A blow to the head is the medical term for a knock to the head, usually from a fall, an accident or during sport, according to the SEUP [1]. The most common symptoms are headache, confusion, brief memory loss, dizziness, nausea, vomiting and drowsiness [1]. Watch your baby closely for the first 24 hours after the knock to spot warning signs [2]. Most head injuries are mild and are not dangerous [2].

Go to the emergency department if your baby is under three months old, if the fall was from more than one metre, or if any of those symptoms appear or their behaviour worries you [4].

q: my 6 month old has started eating food, what should I give first
text:
Around 6 months is the right time to start solid foods, according to the NHS [2]. At first, how much your baby eats matters less than getting them used to eating; they still get most of their energy and nutrients from breast milk or first infant formula [2].

Start with one food at a time, following your family's usual foods, to vary the diet and improve nutrition — never before 4 months, according to the AEP [4]. Iron-rich foods are important, especially if your baby was born prematurely [6].

If your baby was born prematurely, ask your doctor for advice on when to start [2].

text: A high temperature is the body's natural response to fighting an infection, and it is not in itself a sign of how serious the illness is [4]. q: when to start feeding puree to 6 months old
text: At around 6 months, start solid foods alongside breast milk, and move your baby on from puréed or blended foods to mashed, lumpy or finger foods as soon as they can manage them, according to the NHS [2]. Some babies like to start with mashed, lumpy or finger foods, while others need a little longer and prefer smooth foods on a spoon at first — just keep offering lumpy textures and they will get used to it [2]. There is no right or wrong way to feed these first foods; the most important thing is that your baby eats a wide variety of food and gets all the nutrients they need [1]. q: what solids to give first to 6 month baby
text: Introducing solid foods should start when your baby is around 6 months old, according to the NHS [3]. At the beginning, how much they eat matters less than getting used to the idea of eating — they still get most energy and nutrients from breast milk or first infant formula [3]. You can offer purées, mashed foods, cereals and soft finger foods, and let them feed themselves if they prefer; there is no right or wrong way, and there is no more risk of choking when a baby feeds themselves than when spoon-fed [1][2]. Giving a variety of foods from around 6 months helps set up healthier eating later [3]. If your baby was born prematurely, ask your doctor for advice on when to start [3].

q: my 4 year old child has small red bumps on face and neck
text:
Small red bumps on the face and neck can be part of a measles rash, according to the WHO: it usually starts on the face and upper neck and moves down over about three days [6]. The CDC describes it as flat red spots beginning at the hairline that spread down to the neck and body, sometimes with small raised bumps on top [3]. Measles rash appears 3 to 5 days after the first symptoms, which include fever, runny nose, cough and red watery eyes [6].

See a doctor if your child has a high fever, is drowsy or difficult to wake, or has trouble breathing [6].

q: my 1 year old baby body is very hot since morning
text: A fever is a body temperature higher than normal, and it is usually a sign that the body is fighting an infection, according to MedlinePlus [1]. Most fevers are caused by infections, and fever itself is not an illness [1]. For a 12-month-old, any fever is a reason to see a health professional as soon as possible [4]. You can offer plenty of fluids to prevent dehydration, and if the fever is high your doctor may recommend an over-the-counter medicine such as acetaminophen or ibuprofen [1]. Never give aspirin to a child with fever [1].

q: my baby has vomiting and loose motion since morning
text:
Vomiting and loose stools like this are usually caused by a stomach bug, according to the NHS [1]. Diarrhoea usually stops within 5 to 7 days and vomiting in 1 or 2 days [6]. Keep feeding: no need to fast, just smaller amounts more often, and keep breastfeeding as normal or more if your baby wants it [5]. Offer oral rehydration solution, and avoid fruit juice, fizzy drinks and sports drinks, which can make diarrhoea worse [4][5][6]. Do not give children under 12 medicine to stop diarrhoea [6].

See a doctor if your baby is under 3 months and has vomited two or more feeds, is drowsy or floppy, has sunken eyes, cries without tears, is very thirsty or is passing little urine [2].

q: my son has fast breathing with cough

In bronchiolitis, which often starts like a normal cold with cough and mucus, breathing difficulty can appear after 2 to 4 days — faster breathing, irritability, and trouble feeding [3]. While you are on your way, keep your son upright or semi-seated, and offer fluids often in small amounts [7]. q: my 3 year old has fever 102, can I give Calpol
text:
102 °F = 38.9 °C.

Yes, paracetamol (Calpol) can help when a child is distressed or uncomfortable from a high temperature, according to the NHS [3]. Paracetamol and ibuprofen work similarly for fever, and alternating them routinely every 3 to 4 hours is not recommended [1]. Keep your child well hydrated and do not force them to eat [1]. q: can I give ORS to my 1 year old after diarrhea
text: Yes, you can give oral rehydration salts to your 1-year-old after diarrhoea. The WHO lists rehydration with ORS as a key treatment for diarrhoea, and says diarrhoea should be treated with ORS, a solution of clean water, sugar and salt [1][6]. The WHO also lists zinc supplements as a key treatment: they reduce how long the episode lasts by 25% and are associated with a 30% reduction in stool volume [1]. Keep giving nutrient-rich foods, including breast milk, during the episode [1]. See a doctor for persistent diarrhoea, blood in the stool, or signs of dehydration [1].

q: le ha salido un sarpullido rojo por las piernas y le pica
text:
Un sarpullido rojo que pica en las piernas puede ser una urticaria: son placas rojas y elevadas que pican mucho, y en la infancia la mayoría están causadas por una infección, según la SEUP [3]. También puede tratarse de una reacción alérgica, que a veces cursa con picazón y sarpullido, según MedlinePlus [4]. Las picaduras de insectos, como los mosquitos, producen lesiones que pican intensamente y aparecen sobre todo en brazos y piernas, según Ecimed [6].

Conviene consultar al médico si el sarpullido se extiende, no mejora en unos días, se infecta por el rascado o si aparece hinchazón de cara, labios o lengua, o dificultad para respirar [3][5][6].

q: mi hijo tiene conjuntivitis y se le pegan los ojos al despertarse
text:
La conjuntivitis es una inflamación de la parte externa del ojo y del interior del párpado, y suele mejorar en un par de semanas sin tratamiento, según el NHS [5]. Para los párpados pegados al despertar, se pueden limpiar los bordes con agua hervida y fría, usando una gasa limpia distinta para cada ojo [5]. La conjuntivitis infecciosa se contagia con facilidad de una persona a otra, según MedlinePlus [2].

Consulta a tu médico si el niño tiene menos de 30 días, si hay dolor, sensibilidad a la luz o cambios en la visión, o si no mejora en 7 días [1].

Las costillas marcándose al respirar son un signo de dificultad respiratoria que hay que vigilar, según la SEUP [2][4]. q: mi hija se ha caido de un segundo piso pero parece estar bien
banner: 🚨 Con estos síntomas hay que acudir a urgencias hoy, sin esperar. | Motivo: Caída por las escaleras o de más de un metro, o llanto que no se calma tras un golpe: que lo vea un médico hoy
text:
Los síntomas más habituales tras un golpe en la cabeza son dolor de cabeza, confusión, pérdida de memoria transitoria, mareo, náuseas, vómitos y somnolencia, según la SEUP [1]. Es importante vigilar a la niña durante las primeras 24 horas para detectar síntomas de gravedad [2]. Mientras la llevan a valorar, no debe hacer actividad física ni usar pantallas, y se recomienda reposo físico y mental entre 24 y 48 horas [6].

Vigilen en casa y consulten si aparece:

- Dolor de cabeza intenso, progresivo o que no mejora con paracetamol o ibuprofeno [6].
- Vómitos repetidos, desorientación o confusión [6].
- Cambios en el comportamiento, dificultad para hablar o caminar, o salida de sangre o líquido claro por la nariz o los oídos [6].

q: mi bebe tiene 9 meses y todavia no tiene dientes
text:
La erupción de los dientes de leche empieza alrededor de los 6 meses, con los incisivos centrales inferiores, según el manual de pediatría de la PUC de Chile [6]. Que a los 9 meses todavía no le haya salido ninguno puede entrar dentro de la variación normal de cada bebé, así que no hay que alarmarse.

Mientras tanto, conviene revisarle la boca con cuidado: encías, lengua y frenillo lingual, y aprovechar para empezar los cuidados de higiene oral [6].

Consulta a tu pediatra o dentista infantil si a los 12-13 meses sigue sin aparecer ningún diente, o antes si notas encías muy inflamadas o algún problema al comer o al hablar [6].

q: mi hija ha dejado de decir palabras que antes decía
text:
Losing words a child used to say is something to have checked: el proveedor de salud preguntará por la historia del desarrollo y de la familia, hará una exploración neurológica y puede pedir una prueba de audición para ver si la pérdida de audición es la causa [5]. Según MedlinePlus, en los trastornos del habla el niño puede dejar de usar algunos sonidos o cambiarlos, y eso puede hacer que solo la familia le entienda [1][4]. Los hitos del desarrollo no son pautas precisas y hay muchos ritmos normales distintos [6].

Consulta con tu pediatra para que valoren el lenguaje y la audición de tu hija [5].

q: mi hijo de 15 años tiene dolor en el pecho despues de hacer deporte
text: El dolor de pecho tiene muchas causas y, en la mayoría de los casos, no se debe a un problema del corazón [1]. Un dolor que aparece después de hacer ejercicio o de una lesión en el pecho, que empeora al respirar hondo y mejora con el reposo puede ser un esguince o una contractura muscular [1]. También la ansiedad puede provocar presión o dolor en el pecho, junto con palpitaciones, respiración acelerada o sudoración [3]. Conviene que lo vea un médico para valorarlo, sobre todo si el dolor se hace más intenso o no mejora en reposo [1].

q: mi hija se desmayo jugando al futbol pero ahora esta bien
text:
El desmayo o síncope es una pérdida de conocimiento brusca y corta, y suele ocurrir cuando no llega suficiente sangre u oxígeno al cerebro, según la SEUP [1]. El calor, el esfuerzo, el dolor o el miedo son situaciones que lo favorecen [1]. Antes de perder el conocimiento puede haber náuseas, visión borrosa, sudoración o zumbidos, y tras un rato de reposo los niños suelen recuperarse en un par de minutos [2][5].

Conviene que beba más líquidos, sobre todo cuando hace ejercicio, y que se siente o tumbe en cuanto empiece a encontrarse mal [3][5].

Consultad en urgencias si el desmayo ocurrió haciendo ejercicio o esfuerzo, si tardó más de 3-5 minutos en recuperar el conocimiento, o si hubo palpitaciones, dolor en el pecho, sacudidas o pérdida de orina [4].

q: mi bebe esta vomitando y no consigue quedarse con ni siquiera pequeños sorbos
text: Lo más importante es evitar la deshidratación, y para eso las soluciones de rehidratación oral ya preparadas son lo indicado, según la SEUP [3]. Hay que ofrecerlas en dosis pequeñas y tomas frecuentes, para que el bebé las tolere [6]. No uses soluciones caseras ni refrescos comerciales para reponer las pérdidas [3]. Si no consigue retener ni pequeños sorbos, o si tiene mucha sed, llora sin lágrimas, orina poco o tiene los ojos hundidos, hay que ver a un profesional de la salud lo antes posible [3]. En bebés, no mojar los pañales durante 3 horas o más y no tener lágrimas al llorar son también señales de deshidratación [2].

q: cuando se puede empezar con la fruta y la verdura
text:
La fruta y la verdura forman parte de la alimentación normal del niño y se pueden ofrecer cuando come bien y sin forzarle, según la SEUP [1]. En los bebés se mantiene la leche habitual, materna o de fórmula, y en los niños mayores se reintroduce poco a poco su comida de siempre [1]. La fruta y la verdura también ayudan cuando hay estreñimiento, porque aportan fibra [4]. Eso sí, no sustituyas la fruta por zumos, porque tienen poca fibra [4].

Si es un bebé menor de 6 meses, la alimentación sigue siendo solo leche, materna o de fórmula [4].

q: mi hijo es asmatico y se le hunden las costillas al respirar
banner: 🚨 Llama ahora al 112 o acude a urgencias. | Motivo: Dificultad para respirar grave (se marcan las costillas, respira muy rápido, pausas en la respiración, color azulado)
text: El hundimiento del pecho y las costillas al respirar es un signo de dificultad respiratoria que aparece en las crisis asmáticas, según la SEUP [4]. En una crisis asmática, lo indicado es administrar de 2 a 4 pulsaciones de salbutamol con cámara espaciadora, de una en una, y repetir esa dosis a los 10-15 minutos [6]. Si la crisis no cede con el tratamiento en casa, hay que acudir lo antes posible a un centro sanitario, sin olvidar la cámara espaciadora [6]. Mantén al niño en reposo y evita los ambientes con humo de tabaco [6].

Paracetamol para 12 kg:

  – Apiretal, gotas 100 mg/ml: 1.8 ml
  – jarabe 120 mg/5 ml: 7.5 ml
  – jarabe 125 mg/5 ml: 7.2 ml

  – jarabe 160 mg/5 ml: 5.6 ml

La guía admite de 120 a 180 mg; esta es la dosis habitual para la fiebre.
Fuente: AEPap — Guía rápida de dosificación práctica en pediatría (3.ª ed.), tabla analgésicos/antitérmicos.

q: y si no le baja la fiebre le puedo dar dalsy
text: No, no se recomienda alternar paracetamol e ibuprofeno de forma sistemática cada 3-4 horas, según la SEUP [1]. Solo es razonable cambiar de antitérmico si a las 3-4 horas la temperatura sigue alta y el malestar no mejora, según la AEPap [6]. En ese caso, si empezó con paracetamol y no mejora, la próxima dosis puede ser ibuprofeno [6]. Que la fiebre no baje del todo tras un antitérmico es frecuente y no implica mayor gravedad [3]. Vigile su estado general y su color, y consulte si aparecen puntos rojos que no desaparecen al apretarlos [3].

q: mi bebe lleva todo el dia sin hacer pis
banner: 🚨 Con estos síntomas hay que acudir a urgencias hoy, sin esperar. | Motivo: Signos de deshidratación: ojos hundidos, orina poco, boca seca, vómitos persistentes o diarrea abundante >24 h
text: Un bebé puede estar hasta 24 horas sin hacer pis después de la primera micción; pasado ese tiempo, debe mojar los pañales con frecuencia, con orina clara e inodora, según la Junta de Andalucía [6]. Si lleva todo el día sin orinar, eso es uno de los signos que indican que hay que consultar hoy: ojos hundidos, orina escasa, boca seca, vómitos persistentes o diarrea abundante más de 24 horas, según la SEUP [4]. Mientras tanto, ofrécele el pecho o el biberón con normalidad y con más frecuencia si lo pide [1].

q: mi hijo de 2 años tiene 39.5 de fiebre y las manos muy frias
banner: 🚨 Con estos síntomas hay que acudir a urgencias hoy, sin esperar. | Motivo: Manos y pies fríos en un niño con fiebre: puede ser mala circulación, hay que verlo
text: Con fiebre alta, las manos y los pies fríos pueden indicar mala circulación, y eso requiere valoración médica hoy [2]. Mientras tanto, no desabrigues al niño ni le des un baño de agua fría para bajarle la fiebre, y no le abrigues en exceso [2]. Ofrécele líquidos con frecuencia y comida si la quiere, y vigílalo también por la noche [6]. Puedes darle paracetamol o ibuprofeno si está molesto, comprobando antes en el prospecto que es adecuado para su edad [6]. Consulta también si tiene manchas en la piel que no desaparecen al presionarlas, está decaído o poco reactivo, o le cuesta respirar [1].

q: mi hijo tiene diarrea pero quiere comer normal
text: Sí, en general puede comer lo que le apetezca: lo más importante durante una diarrea es evitar la deshidratación, y las soluciones de rehidratación oral se ofrecen en dosis pequeñas y tomas frecuentes, según la SEUP [3]. La gastroenteritis suele mejorar sola, con reposo y abundantes líquidos y electrolitos, según MedlinePlus [5]. No le des medicamentos para la diarrea o los vómitos sin consultar con su pediatra [2]. Consulta pronto si rechaza comer o beber, si está irritable o somnoliento, si orina poco o no moja los pañales durante 3 horas o más, o si la diarrea dura más de un día en un niño pequeño [1][2].
